formalizations.formalization: ∀ (a : Point) (b : Point) (c : Point) (d : Point) (e : Point) (AB : Line) (CD : Line) (BC : Line) (AE : Line), ((formParallelogram a b c d AB CD BC AE) ∧ (formTriangle e b c BC AE CD)) → (Triangle.area △ a:b:c + Triangle.area △ a:c:d = 2 * Triangle.area △ e:b:c)
formalizations.full_output: theorem example_thm (a b c d e : Point) (AB CD BC AE : Line) (h1 : formParallelogram a b c d AB CD BC AE) (h2 : formTriangle e b c BC AE CD) : Triangle.area △ a:b:c + Triangle.area △ a:c:d = 2 * Triangle.area △ e:b:c := by

formalizations.formalization: ∀ (a : Point) (b : Point) (c : Point) (d : Point) (e : Point) (AB : Line) (CD : Line) (AE : Line) (BC : Line), ((formParallelogram a b c d AB CD AE BC) ∧ (formTriangle a b c AB BC AE) ∧ (formTriangle e b c BC AE BC) ∧ (Triangle.area △ e:b:c = (Triangle.area △ a:b:c) / 2)) → (Triangle.area △ a:b:c + Triangle.area △ c:d:a = 2 * Triangle.area △ e:b:c)
formalizations.full_output:
theorem parallelogram_double_triangle (a b c d e : Point) (AB CD AE BC : Line)
  (h1 : formParallelogram a b c d AB CD AE BC)
  (h2 : formTriangle a b c AB BC AE)
  (h3 : formTriangle e b c BC AE BC)
  (h4 : Triangle.area △ e:b:c = (Triangle.area △ a:b:c) / 2) :
  Triangle.area △ a:b:c + Triangle.area △ c:d:a = 2 * Triangle.area △ e:b:c := by

reference_formalization: ∀ (a b c d e : Point) (AE BC AB CD BE CE : Line), formParallelogram a d b c AE BC AB CD ∧ formTriangle e b c BE BC CE ∧ e.onLine AE ∧ ¬(AE.intersectsLine BC) → (Triangle.area △ a:b:c : ℝ) + (Triangle.area △ a:c:d) = (Triangle.area △ e:b:c) + (Triangle.area △ e :b :c)
nl_statement: If a parallelogram has the same base as a triangle, and is between the same parallels, then the parallelogram is double (the area) of the triangle. For let parallelogram $ABCD$ have the same base $BC$ as triangle $EBC$, and let it be between the same parallels, $BC$ and $AE$. I say that  parallelogram $ABCD$ is double (the area) of triangle $BEC$.  <prf> So parallelogram $ABCD$ is also double (the area) of triangle $EBC$.Thus, if a parallelogram has the same base as a triangle, and is between the same parallels, then the parallelogram is double (the area) of the triangle.
